answer: Each identity runs a permitted banding station: mist nets in one grove, surveyed coordinates, a block of serialised federal bands. Each epoch the seed names a net lane and a ninety-minute dawn slot; the agent files a capture record with the band number from its block, species, wing chord and a photo of the banded leg. Bands sharing a permit or bander fold into one vote, and the lab ledger refuses any reused number. Kit and permit cost $1,900 a station, so a thousand clones need a thousand dawns and a sparrow in hand. A band is riveted to one leg, as a comet's orbit belongs to one nucleus.
